Claimant fell down and sustained injuries.
Despite treatment at Government Hospital, Tavaragera and Lifeline Hospital, Hubballi, she did NC: 2026:KHC-D:3411 HC-KAR not recover fully and sustained loss of earning capacity.

9. It was firstly submitted, title of Ex.R.1 itself would reveal that it was not an 'act liability only policy' but was "two wheelers certificate-cum-policy schedule" thereby indicating that it was comprehensive.
Therefore, absolving liability of insurer would be unsustainable.
On quantum, it was submitted, claimant was 50 years of age working as tailor and earning Rs.8,000/- per month.

However, Tribunal considered meager monthly income of Rs.3,000/- and assessed inadequate compensation.

However,
Tribunal considered only 8% as functional disability and awarded inadequate compensation.
Learned counsel for appellant submitted that, even compensation awarded towards pain and suffering and loss of amenities were on lower side and sought enhancement.
On said grounds sought for modification of award.
11. On other hand, Sri Rajashekhar S. Arani, learned counsel appearing for respondent no.3-insurer opposed appeal.
It was submitted, admittedly insurance subscribed to by claimant/owner of vehicle was an 'act liability only policy' and no specific premium was paid to cover risk of pillion rider.
Under above circumstances, Tribunal had validly absolved insurer and held liable on owner to pay compensation.
On said grounds sought for dismissal.

sentences.text:
Heard learned counsel, perused impugned judgment and award and certified copies of pleadings,
depositions and exhibits made available by learned counsel for appellant.
13. This appeal by claimant against dismissal of claim petition against respondent no.3-insurer as well as for enhancement of compensation.

Therefore points that would arise for consideration are :
"i. Whether Tribunal was justified in dismissing claim petition against insurer?
ii. Whether claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation as prayed?"
14. Point no.1 : Contention on liability is primarily based on submission that Ex.R.1 was not an 'act liability only policy' but a 'package policy'.
However, to know extent of coverage under a policy, one need not advert to title of policy but its terms.
Coverage of risk of owner, driver and pillion rider in private vehicle is not statutory/compulsory.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3411 HC-KAR Perusal of Ex.R.1-insurance policy would reveal that there is no separate premium paid for covering risk of un named passenger or pillion rider.

In view of above,
there would be no scope for interference with finding of Tribunal on liability.
Accordingly, Point no.1 is answered in affirmative.
15. Point no.2 :
As per claimant, he was 50 years of age working as tailor and earning Rs.8,000/- per month.
However, same was not substantiated with specific material.
In absence, Tribunal would be justified assessing it notionally.
Notional income for 2007 date of accident would be Rs.4,000/-.
Therefore, same as to be considered.

16. Indeed as submitted by learned counsel for claimant, PW.2-Dr.H.Ramakrishna assessed permanent physical disability of claimant at 25% to affected limb and at 12.5% to whole body and issued Ex.P.91-disability certificate.

Perusal of deposition of PW.2 reveals his observation on clinical examination as follows:
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3411 HC-KAR "Walks with support, Left Limb appears to be shortened, Left Limb measures of about 84 cm, Right Limb measures of about 86 cm,
Left Limb shortened by 2 cm, Left Thigh measures of about 44 cm, Right Thigh measures of about 46 cm, Girth of the Left Thigh is reduced by 2 cm due to wasting of the muscles, left Calf measures of about 22 cm, Right Calf measures of about 25 cm,
Left Calf Reduced by 2 cm due to wasting of Muscle, Flexon of the Left Hip beyond 90 degree not possible, Difficulty in squatting & Climbing the steps, Difficulty in walking."
17. It is seen that said deposition is not discredited in cross-examination.
When PW2 has assessed functional disability to whole body disability at 12.5%.
Tribunal erred in not noting that fracture sustained is of femur and occupation of claimant is as tailor.

Therefore, Tribunal would not be Pramila W/O Narahariyappa vs Ravikumar S/O Ramanna Belkondi on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13498501/
5 justified in assessing loss of earning capacity at 8%.

sentences.text: It would be appropriate to consider loss of earning capacity at 12.5%.
Multiplier applicable to age 50 years would be '11'.

Thus compensation towards loss of future income would be Rs.66,000/- (Rs.4,000 X 12.5% X 12 X 11)
- 10 - NC: 2026:KHC-D:3411 HC-KAR 18.
Considering fact that, claimant sustained fracture of femur which is structural bone, award of Rs.20,000/- towards 'pain and suffering' would be grossly inadequate, same is enhanced by Rs.40,000/-.
Likewise award of Rs.5,000/- towards 'loss of amenities' would also be grossly inadequate, same is enhanced to Rs.35,000/-.

19. In view of re-assessment of monthly income and considering 3 months as period of lay of on account of fractural injury, compensation towards loss of earning during laid up period requires to be awarded Rs.12,000/-.
Award of Rs.5,000/- towards diet and other incidental charges is up held.
Award of Rs.1,54,418/- towards medical expenses is upheld as there is complete reimbursement of bills produced.
Thus appellant is entitled to receive compensation of Rs.3,12,418/- as against Rs.2,22,098/- awarded by Tribunal.
Consequently, point no.2 is answered partly in affirmative as above.

Accordingly, following:
- 11 - NC: 2026:KHC-D:3411 HC-KAR ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) Claimant is held entitled for re-assessed compensation of Rs.3,12,418/- with interest at 6% per annum from date of claim petition, till deposit.
(iii) Dismissal of claim petition against respondent no.3-insurer is up held.
(iv) Respondent no.2-owner shall deposit enhanced compensation before Tribunal within 8 weeks from date of receipt of certified copy of judgment.

Sd/-
